question: How is drinking alcohol and driving classified?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem,b:Safe if you have only had a few drinks,c:A minor traffic safety problem
note: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is a serious safety issue and greatly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to:
options: a:Other drivers already in the intersection,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:Pedestrians only if they are in a crosswalk
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians and bicyclists in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on:
options: a:Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic,b:Whether there is a stop sign present,c:Whether you used your turn signal
note: The gap needed to cross or turn depends on road surface, weather, and the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.

question: Which factors affect your vehicle's braking distance?
options: a:Only the number of passengers.,b:Only the age of the vehicle.,c:Vehicle speed,d:Only the color of the vehicle.
note: Braking distance depends on how fast you are traveling, the state of your brakes and tires, and road surface conditions such as wetness or ice.

question: If you hit an unattended parked car and can't find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Stay until the police arrive,b:Assume you have done enough and leave,c:Leave a written note with your name
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle, leave a written notice with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident if the owner cannot be located.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by which color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:Green lines.,c:White lines.,d:Red lines.
note: White lines (solid or broken) are used to separate lanes moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must the driver produce?
options: a:Only their license.,b:Their driver license,c:Only proof of insurance.,d:Only proof of registration.
note: Drivers must present their license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance when requested by law enforcement.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:At any time regardless of conditions,b:Only during daylight hours,c:When it is safe to change lanes
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when safe.

question: When you reach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Come to a full stop,d:Drive through if the intersection seems clear.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding the right-of-way, just like a stop sign.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross,b:Always stop at the curb before crossing,c:Possibly run into the street without looking
note: Children can act unpredictably; reduce speed and be prepared to stop at any time.

question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane indicate the boundaries of:
options: a:A bicycle lane,b:A pedestrian crosswalk,c:A no-passing zone for vehicles only
note: Two solid white lines can mark a crosswalk; drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks.

question: Taking drugs along with alcohol generally:
options: a:Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone,b:Lessens the effect of alcohol on driving ability,c:Increases the risk of causing a crash
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) increases impairment and crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.,b:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,c:Back up on the exit ramp.,d:Signal and cross multiple lanes at once to get back.
note: Do not stop or back up on the highway; proceed to the next exit and safely turn around to return to the desired exit.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:They must use the bicycle lane,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles,c:They are limited to half a lane
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane just like other vehicles and should be treated accordingly.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Keep accelerating to reach the shoulder quickly,b:Do not immediately use your brakes; take your foot off the gas,c:Immediately stomp on the brakes
note: Take your foot off the gas, avoid sudden braking, gradually slow, then steer to a safe place to stop.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Drive directly behind them very close.,b:Always pass on the right,c:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating; do not remain beside them for extended periods.,d:Flash your lights to get their attention.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots at the sides and rear; avoid lingering alongside and give them plenty of space when passing.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that has no active signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if you see or hear a train,c:Assume all crossings have signals and proceed normally
note: At unprotected crossings slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if one is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A double solid yellow centerline down a two-lane road means:
options: a:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:A place safe to park.,b:Dangerous — always look and listen for trains.,c:Safe to cross without looking.
note: Railroad crossings are hazardous; always look both ways, listen, and obey signals or flaggers before crossing.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The beginning of a reduced speed zone.,b:The area with more children present.,c:The end of the reduced speed school zone.
note: The 'End school zone' sign marks the point where the special school zone speed limit and restrictions end.

question: Why must drivers be more cautious at night?
options: a:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark,b:There is a larger volume of traffic at night,c:Traffic moves faster at night
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards; headlights must be used from half hour after sunset to half hour before sunrise.

question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is separated by what color lines?
options: a:White lines,b:Red lines,c:Yellow lines
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate traffic moving the same direction.

question: When your visibility decreases, your first response should be to:
options: a:Turn on your windshield wipers,b:Reduce your speed,c:Turn on your headlights
note: Reducing speed gives you more time to react when visibility is limited or road conditions are hazardous.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash mean?
options: a:Drivers should come to a complete stop,b:Some drivers must yield,c:The action shown is forbidden
note: A red circle with a slash over a symbol indicates that the depicted action is prohibited.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reduce visibility by reflecting off moisture.

question: Which recommendation does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep the windshield clean,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility,c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle
note: Carrying a flashlight is not one of the primary measures for safe night driving; the focus should be on clean windshield and avoiding dark-tint that reduces visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection simultaneously with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle whose driver honks first,b:The vehicle approaching from the right,c:The vehicle approaching from the left
note: At intersections of similar roads without controls, yield to traffic coming from your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass another vehicle when:
options: a:On a hill or curve,b:You are driving at the speed limit,c:You are approaching an intersection with wide visibility
note: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, or when sight distance is limited.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do?
options: a:Always leave the injured where they are.,b:Not move the injured unnecessarily. Keep the injured warm and administer first aid.,c:Moved the injured away from the scene immediately.
note: Avoid moving injured persons unless necessary; keep them warm, control severe bleeding, and wait for professional medical help.

question: What do regulatory signs tell drivers?
options: a:That the area is especially dangerous,b:What drivers must or must not do,c:They are warning signs (diamond-shaped
note: Regulatory signs instruct drivers about legal requirements (speed limits, turn restrictions, etc.) and are often rectangular with black on white markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the posted speed limit sign represent?
options: a:The exact safe speed for all drivers.,b:A recommended speed for heavy traffic only.,c:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: The posted limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust downward for adverse conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield if a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield to the driver,b:Whoever started moving last must yield,c:The driver must yield to the pedestrian
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in intersections without traffic signals to prevent collisions.

question: When should you reduce speed due to road or environmental conditions?
options: a:Only when you see a police car,b:Only when entering a highway with traffic,c:On narrow or winding roads
note: Slow down in areas or conditions that reduce safety: narrow/winding roads, intersections, crossings, and slippery surfaces.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, you should:
options: a:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent the emergency vehicle from passing,b:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel (pull to side when safe),c:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle
note: You must allow emergency vehicles using sirens or lights a clear path; pull over to the side and stop if it is safe to do so.

question: What is the correct method for backing a vehicle safely?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing, rather than relying only on mirrors.,b:Rely only on mirrors and backup cameras.,c:Open the driver's door and back slowly while stepping out.
note: Before backing, check behind the vehicle and while reversing, turn and look through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what is your immediate duty?
options: a:Continue driving and report it later.,b:Stop immediately,c:Hide to avoid responsibility.,d:Only help if you caused the crash.
note: Stop, provide assistance as necessary, and notify law enforcement; do not move injured people unless required for safety and you know how.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle approaches with lights, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop,b:Turn on your flashers and continue driving,c:Speed up and exit quickly
note: On one-way streets, move toward the nearest edge of the road and stop for emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out due to power failure at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Park and wait for power to return,b:Turn on your hazards and proceed without stopping,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield in turn
note: Yield as you would at a four-way stop: first to arrive, then to the right, proceeding with caution when it's your turn.

question: When may a driver with a probationary license use a telecommunications device while driving?
options: a:Only to call 911 in an emergency,b:When they are a high school graduate,c:Texting but not talking on the phone
note: In Indiana, probationary license holders (under 21) may only use a phone while driving to contact 911 for emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should end up in:
options: a:The left lane of the one-way street (closest to the lane you came from),b:The center of the one-way street,c:The right lane of the one-way street
note: Complete the left turn into the lane closest to the lane you left — typically the left lane of the one-way street.

question: What does a red arrow signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and then proceed when clear without waiting for a green signal.,b:Slow and proceed through the intersection.,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped until the signal changes to a green arrow or circular green light.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is the driver's responsibility?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is looking at their phone.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and take all reasonable actions to avoid striking them.,c:Only yield when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,d:Proceed unless the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must do everything reasonable to avoid hitting pedestrians and must yield even if the pedestrian is crossing where they should not be.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street,b:Close to the left side of the street,c:As close to the right side of the road as possible
note: Before making a right turn, move as far right as practicable and do not cut across lanes when turning.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A solid yellow light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A steady green light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing yellow light means to slow down and proceed with caution, being prepared to stop if necessary.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when parking.,b:Only when backing up.,c:Before changing lanes
note: Any time you plan to move laterally in traffic—changing lanes or turning—glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use the entrance ramp to merge onto a crowded freeway?
options: a:Always stop before merging.,b:Yield to emergency vehicles on the ramp.,c:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.
note: Use the ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and then merge when there is a safe gap.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving generally have what level of control?
options: a:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,c:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time, reducing driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:
options: a:Refuse to let other cars pass you,b:Pull off the road and let traffic pass when safe,c:Decrease your speed further
note: If you are impeding traffic on a two-lane two-way road, pull off when safe to allow others to pass.

question: What does an orange traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A railroad crossing ahead.,b:A school zone.,c:Road work or maintenance ahead.
note: Orange signs with black symbols or lettering warn of construction, maintenance, or other temporary work zones.

question: When you are near heavy trucks, others should allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and accelerate; smaller vehicles should avoid lingering in blind spots and allow extra space.

question: What is the most important speed-management rule for curves?
options: a:Maintain or increase speed as you enter the curve.,b:Slow down before you enter the curve.,c:Brake hard while in the curve.
note: Because inertia can push your vehicle outward, slow down before entering a curve to maintain control.

question: What can happen if a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:They are immune from traffic stops.,b:They can be ticketed like other road users.,c:They will always receive only a warning.,d:They are always excused because they are bicyclists.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and can be cited for traffic violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic light means what?
options: a:Merging traffic,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: What is the correct action when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?
options: a:Stop in the middle of the intersection and wait.,b:Try to reach your destination before it arrives.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop,d:Continue driving but attempt to remain out of its way.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping when safe; if in an intersection, clear it before pulling over.

question: Before starting the ignition, what safety action should you take?
options: a:Only check that backseat passengers have buckled.,b:Make sure the radio is off.,c:Start the engine and then buckle up.,d:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are restrained.
note: Develop a routine of buckling your seat belt and making sure passengers are belted before switching on the ignition.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Take the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Proceed normally.
note: Yield and be prepared to stop for blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog; always exercise extra caution.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood it generally:
options: a:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly,b:Makes you less confident,c:Slows your reaction time
note: Alcohol slows your reactions, reduces perception, and impairs judgment and coordination.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Only exchange insurance information and leave,b:Continue driving to the nearest police station,c:Stop
note: Stop if possible, provide aid, call emergency services for injuries, and report the crash to law enforcement when required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A single broken yellow centerline down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and you may pass when it is safe,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed,c:You are not permitted to pass
note: A broken yellow centerline means passing is permitted for vehicles in either direction when safe.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Never; keep the same distance at all times.,b:When following a large vehicle that blocks your vision,c:Only when following a motorcycle.,d:When traffic is light and visibility is good.
note: Increase following distance behind large vehicles, in bad weather, when behind motorcycles or bicycles, and whenever you need extra reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Increase your speed,c:Come to a complete stop
note: A flashing yellow warns of potential hazards; slow down and be prepared to yield.

question: How long do points assessed for traffic violations remain on your Indiana driving record?
options: a:Six months,b:Two years,c:Nine months
note: Points remain on your driving record for two years from the date of conviction under Indiana's point system.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the proper immediate response?
options: a:Turn off the ignition while driving at highway speed.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure to the brake,c:Shift into park immediately while moving.,d:Reach down to manually lift the pedal while keeping speed.
note: Keep control, shift to neutral, brake steadily, move to a safe location, then turn off the engine once stopped.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light in which situation?
options: a:Only if turning left.,b:If you are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow.,c:Only if you are speeding up to clear the intersection.,d:If you see pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through cautiously to clear it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Only inexperienced drivers are endangered by speed differences.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:Speed has no effect on crash severity.
note: Driving well below the flow of traffic can create hazards by prompting risky passing maneuvers; speed management is important for safety.

question: Which of these about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season,b:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe
note: Do not use cruise control in snow or slippery conditions; winter driving requires extra caution and vehicle maintenance.

question: What is the first thing you should adjust when getting into a car?
options: a:Your seat position so you can see and reach controls comfortably,b:Your rearview mirror,c:Your seat belt
note: Adjust your seat first to ensure good visibility and control reach, then set mirrors, steering wheel, and fasten your seat belt.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crash risk?
options: a:Just tell someone 'No thanks,b:Call a taxi only after you begin drinking,c:Decide before drinking that you will not drive
note: Deciding ahead of time not to drive after drinking is the only reliable way to avoid alcohol-related risks, since alcohol impairs judgment.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Make every effort to get out of their way and avoid engaging them.,b:Stare at the driver to intimidate them.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: If confronted by an aggressive driver, avoid confrontation and move out of their way when safe to reduce the risk of escalation.

question: Guide signs that show directions and distances are what color?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide or destination signs have a green background and give directional and mileage information.

question: What is the most common color for general warning signs?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what applies to turning vehicles?
options: a:You may still turn in the arrow's direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn at all.,c:You retain right-of-way to turn without yielding.
note: When a green arrow becomes a circular green, turning vehicles must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is illegal to drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:Driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic,b:You are in heavy construction zone traffic,c:Only when driving in rural areas
note: Driving unreasonably slow so as to impede traffic is unlawful and may cause citations.

question: What must a driver do at a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Merge to the right lane.,c:Accelerate through if no other cars are present.,d:Stop
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop fully, yield, and proceed when the way is clear.

question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline where there is a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turning wheels away from the curb helps prevent your vehicle from rolling into traffic if it moves.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road ahead,b:Look straight ahead into the lights,c:Turn on and flash your high beams
note: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its lights, glance toward the right edge of your lane to avoid being momentarily blinded.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop every time.,b:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,c:Speed up to get through first.,d:Leave at least one-half of the traveled portion of the road to the oncoming vehicle.
note: On narrow roads you must allow oncoming vehicles at least half of the main-traveled portion of the road so both can pass safely.

question: How can you reduce the need to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look far ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to warn others.,c:Drive in the leftmost lane only.
note: Scanning ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you time to react to hazards without sudden stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach an open (uncontrolled) intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who honks first,b:The driver on the left,c:The driver on the right
note: At intersections with no signals or signs, yield to the vehicle on your right when you arrive at the same time.

question: If you are angry after an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself while driving.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before starting your drive.,c:Drive fast to let off steam.,d:Immediately begin your commute to get home quicker.
note: If emotionally upset, pause and calm down before driving; anger impairs judgment and increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to slow for a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.,b:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
note: Do not reduce speed on the main freeway; wait until you are on the exit ramp to slow down safely.

question: When may you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Only in an emergency,b:If you turn on your hazard lights,c:If no part of your vehicle is on the road
note: Stopping on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except for emergencies.

question: If an oncoming car has its high beams on and blinds you, you should:
options: a:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs,b:Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes,c:Flash your lights at the oncoming driver
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded and keep control until the car passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and exit the vehicle,c:Get your paperwork out and wave it at the officer
note: Remain in the vehicle with hands visible, and wait for the officer to request your license and registration.

question: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren, a driver must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and turn on four-way flashers,b:Pull to the right and slow down only,c:Pull to the right and stop
note: You must drive to the right side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:Human error,c:New drivers
note: Most crashes result from human error—mistakes, inattention, or poor decisions—rather than just weather or vehicle factors.

question: What do pennant-shaped roadside signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs (pointing left) indicate the start of a no-passing zone on two-lane roads.

question: What must drivers do when approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Pass cautiously if no children appear to be present.,c:Sound the horn and pass on the left.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its stop arm extended, all approaching traffic in both directions must stop until the arm is withdrawn and children are clear.

question: A downward-pointing triangular traffic sign indicates:
options: a:School zone,b:Construction zone,c:Yield to other traffic
note: A downward-pointing triangle is a yield sign, meaning slow down and yield to cross traffic or pedestrians.

question: Who is required by Indiana law to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:Only the driver.,b:Only occupants under age 18.,c:Only front-seat occupants.,d:All occupants of a vehicle equipped with seat belts.
note: Indiana law requires all occupants in a vehicle that has seat belts to use them while the vehicle is in motion.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Not cross the centerline at any time,b:Use the shoulder to pass if necessary,c:Move into the oncoming traffic lane only when it is safe and legal to do so
note: Passing on two-lane, two-way roads requires entering the opposing lane and only doing so when you can complete the pass safely and legally.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal,b:Apply the parking brake,c:Firmly pump the brake pedal
note: First ease off the accelerator; if further slowing is needed, apply brakes gently to avoid skidding.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop,b:Ignore it if you don't see a train,c:Continue at the same speed unless gates are down
note: Slow, look, and be ready to stop at railroad crossings; if lights flash or gates are down, stop 15–50 feet from the tracks.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement, what is the correct way to return to the road?
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately.,b:Slow down gradually,c:Turn the wheel sharply and jerk back onto the pavement.,d:Speed up and bounce back onto pavement.
note: Reduce speed gently while keeping control, then when safe steer slowly back onto the pavement; do not make sudden jerks or braking.

question: What do round signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:School zones ahead.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round signs are used to warn of upcoming railroad crossings; approach with extra caution and be prepared to stop.

question: What is required when you encounter an emergency vehicle using lights and sirens?
options: a:Speed up to pass the emergency vehicle.,b:Ignore the lights if you are in a hurry.,c:Yield the right-of-way and follow any instructions given by the emergency personnel.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using lights and sirens and obey any instructions they give; do not obstruct them.

question: What steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal as you begin the lane change without looking,b:Only check your blind spot by turning your head,c:Signal early, check mirrors, and check your blind spot
note: Before changing lanes, signal early, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,b:Signal only when driving at night.,c:Always signal your intentions when changing lanes
note: You must always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb so other road users can anticipate your actions.

question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection.,b:Ignore it if no other vehicles are present.,c:Slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection.,d:Speed up to get through before it turns red.
note: A steady yellow indicates the signal will soon turn red; stop if it is safe to do so, otherwise proceed if already in the intersection.

question: Which behavior best describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times,b:Looks for and anticipates the actions of other drivers,c:Travels at a constant speed
note: A defensive driver watches others, anticipates hazards, and takes steps to avoid collisions.

question: When driving in fog, which actions improve safety?
options: a:Do not use your high beam headlights.,b:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.,c:All of the above.,d:Use low beam headlights to better see the road ahead.
note: In fog, reduce speed, use low beams (not high beams), and drive cautiously to compensate for reduced visibility.

question: At a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Stop only if a train is visible.,b:Cross immediately to avoid delays.,c:Prepare to yield to any approaching train and never cross unless you can see clearly that all tracks are clear.
note: If there are no gates or lights, look and listen for trains on all tracks and make sure there is room to clear the crossing before proceeding.

question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Ignore traffic around you if mirrors look clear.,b:Change lanes without signaling to be faster.,c:Check side and rearview mirrors
note: Before you change lanes, use mirrors, signal your intention, and check blind spots to ensure the lane is clear.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You must come to a complete stop before turning,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You should merge into the lane of the arrow first
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: When are roads most slippery after rain begins?
options: a:The day after it rains.,b:After it has been raining for several hours.,c:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Oil and other residues rise to the surface when rain first begins, making pavement especially slippery during the first 10–15 minutes.

question: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means:
options: a:A stop sign,b:A hospital sign,c:A speed limit sign
note: An octagonal sign is always a stop sign; you must come to a complete stop at it.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact
note: Stay calm, avoid confrontation, do not make eye contact or gestures, and try to put distance between you and the aggressive driver.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to clear the street.,b:Slow down but continue through the intersection.,c:Pull safely to the right curb and stop until you can locate the vehicle.,d:Keep driving until you actually see it.
note: When you hear but cannot see an emergency vehicle, safely pull over and stop so you can determine its location and let it pass.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign typically:
options: a:Alerts you to school zones,b:Indicates public recreation areas,c:Warns of existing or possible hazards ahead
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of potential hazards or road conditions that require attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:High speeds.,c:Clear weather.,d:Night driving only.
note: Driving at higher speeds increases stopping distance and the energy involved in a crash, greatly raising crash severity.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Passengers when they are on long trips,b:All occupants of the vehicle,c:The person driving the car only
note: All occupants should wear seat belts; unbelted people can be thrown and cause injuries to themselves and others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Speed up and go first.,c:Ignore it and drive through.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Keep the same following distance as in dry conditions.,b:Roads are often most slippery soon after rain begins,c:Turn off your headlights to prevent glare.,d:Wet roads never cause hydroplaning.
note: Road surfaces can be especially slick immediately after rain begins because oil and dirt mix with water; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: If you hear a siren from behind while on the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are without signaling.,b:Speed up to get out of the way.,c:Safely pull over to the right and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.,d:Turn into the opposing lane to clear a path.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching from behind, create a clear path by pulling over to the right and stopping if safe to do so; if in heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can clear the way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed to the next exit and return on surface streets to your destination.,b:Make a U-turn across the median.,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,d:Stop and ask another driver for help.
note: Do not back up or cross the median; go to the next exit and safely return to the missed exit from surface roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.
note: Do not make last-minute turns or lane changes; continue to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:Alcohol always helps the medicine work better.,b:The medicine will cancel out the alcohol.,c:The combination can multiply the effects and increase impairment.
note: Mixing alcohol with medications can greatly increase impairment and unpredictably intensify side effects of both substances.

question: What type of sign warns drivers about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Warning signs,b:Regulatory signs,c:Information signs
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions and should be followed for safety.

question: What can result when alcohol is consumed together with other drugs?
options: a:They have no additional effect.,b:They always cancel each other out.,c:They make you sober faster.,d:The combined effects can increase impairment and be more dangerous than either alone.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can intensify impairment of judgment, reaction time, and coordination, increasing driving danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left if two arrive at once.,b:The driver who arrived last.,c:The driver who arrived first.
note: Vehicles stop from all directions; the first to arrive should proceed first. If two arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has right-of-way.

question: The impairment caused by lack of sleep is most like the impairment from:
options: a:Alcohol,b:Amphetamines,c:Anger
note: Fatigue can impair driving much like alcohol does; e.g., 18 hours awake approximates a 0.05% BAC in impairment.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as:
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: Approach a flashing red signal by coming to a complete stop and yielding to other traffic and pedestrians.

question: What colors identify signs that show distance to upcoming highway exits?
options: a:Green with white letters,b:Yellow with black letters,c:Red with white letters
note: Guide signs that show destinations and distances are green with white letters or symbols.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio reliably prevents drowsiness,b:Drowsy drivers can perform as poorly as drunk drivers and may appear intoxicated,c:Drinking strong coffee permanently restores full alertness
note: Drowsiness can impair driving similar to alcohol; simple measures like windows or radio are usually insufficient to prevent fatigue-related impairment.

question: A person walking with a white cane or using a guide dog is usually:
options: a:Part of a traffic study.,b:A traffic enforcement officer.,c:A blind or visually impaired pedestrian.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind or using a guide dog or white cane.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing tracks that has no signals or gates, what should you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way so proceed regardless.,b:Make sure there is space ahead for your vehicle to clear the tracks without stopping.,c:You may stop on the tracks if necessary.,d:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.
note: Before driving onto tracks without active warnings, ensure there is enough room to fully clear the tracks so you won't be stuck waiting on them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal behavior corresponds to stopping, yielding, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid green light
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when safe — same as a stop sign.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only if no oncoming traffic is present.,b:Yes,c:No — you may not cross a double solid yellow line to pass
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; crossing them is allowed only to turn into or out of driveways or designated entrances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Is not required to stop.,b:Stop at the point nearest the intersection where you can see approaching traffic without entering the roadway.,c:Is required to slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.
note: Stop at the nearest point before the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view; do not enter the intersection to improve your sight line.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are only found in construction zones.,b:Provide information for drivers.,c:Are usually not important.
note: Pavement markings inform drivers about lane positioning, passing permissions, and upcoming roadway conditions.

question: A red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Always come to a full stop.,c:Slow and yield to vehicles or pedestrians; be prepared to stop.
note: A triangular yield sign means you must reduce speed and yield the right-of-way; stop only if necessary.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings must be treated how by drivers?
options: a:Must always be obeyed.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Pavement markings, signals, and signs control traffic and must be obeyed at all times to ensure safety and order.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages while on a public road or highway?
options: a:Only if you are not driving.,b:Never — consuming or possessing open alcohol on a public road is prohibited.,c:Only if you are seated in the back of a vehicle.
note: Indiana law prohibits consuming or possessing open alcoholic beverages on public roads; open container laws apply to areas normally occupied by driver or passengers.

question: A load that extends more than how far beyond a vehicle's rear must be flagged during daylight?
options: a:One foot,b:Two feet,c:Four feet
note: If a load sticks out more than four feet past the rear, it must be marked with a red flag (at least 12 inches square) in clear daylight.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed only when safe.,b:Slow down but do not stop.,c:Proceed with caution without stopping.
note: A flashing red signal has the same requirement as a stop sign: stop completely and proceed when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic if there is no gap.,b:Assume they have the right-of-way.,c:Signal only after entering the road.,d:Yield to drivers already on the public road.
note: Yield to vehicles already using the public roadway and merge safely when there is an adequate gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a red light you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield to pedestrians and cross traffic before turning,b:Honk at nearby pedestrians before turning,c:Turn without stopping if the lane is clear
note: You may turn right on red only after a full stop and after yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, unless posted otherwise.

question: Regarding small children riding in vehicles, which is correct?
options: a:They may be safely held by a strong adult,b:They may stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle,c:They must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint or safety seat
note: Children who are too small for regular seat belts must be secured in an approved child restraint appropriate for their size and age.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance must you signal before making a turn in most situations?
options: a:350 feet,b:200 feet,c:120 yards
note: You must signal at least 200 feet before making a lane change or turn; at speeds above 50 mph signal at least 300 feet.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:All of the above,b:Only body weight,c:Only the amount of food in the stomach
note: Blood alcohol concentration depends on how much alcohol is consumed, how much time passes between drinks, body weight, and food in the stomach.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to turn green.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you should slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution; a full stop is not required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left,b:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Turn on your car radio,b:Slow down,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch
note: Schedule regular rest stops to prevent drowsiness and stay alert on long drives.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do to warn other drivers?
options: a:Use only parking lights.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,c:Use your emergency flashers and keep low-beam headlights on.,d:Stand behind your vehicle with a flashlight.
note: If you must stop at night, turn on hazards and leave low-beam headlights on so other motorists can see your vehicle clearly.

question: What is the legal status of texting while driving in Indiana?
options: a:It is legal only when stopped at a light.,b:It is allowed for drivers over 21.,c:It is illegal to type or read a text or email while driving,d:It is always legal.
note: Indiana prohibits typing or reading texts/emails while driving; only use for emergency communications is exempt.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It causes immediate engine failure,b:It causes your tires to wear faster,c:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger area leading to poisoning
note: A leaking exhaust can introduce carbon monoxide into the cabin, which is poisonous and potentially lethal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are drivers required to stop?
options: a:Only when a traffic officer orders you to stop,b:Only at stop signs,c:At stop signs
note: Drivers must stop at stop signs, red or flashing red lights, and whenever a traffic officer directs them to stop.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before changing lanes called?
options: a:An unnecessary action,b:A bad driving habit,c:A good driving habit
note: Checking blind spots by looking over your shoulder is an important complement to mirror checks when changing lanes or merging.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that may affect safety, what should you do?
options: a:Drive slower until you can fix it.,b:Wait until you can afford it.,c:Have it repaired as soon as possible.
note: Any defect that could affect safe operation should be corrected promptly before driving the vehicle if possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind while going uphill, what should you remember?
options: a:You are always allowed to pass on the uphill.,b:The truck will be going the posted speed.,c:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
note: Large trucks may travel more slowly, especially uphill; be cautious and avoid unsafe passing when visibility is limited.

question: A pentagonal (five-sided) sign indicates:
options: a:No passing zone,b:A school zone or school crossing,c:Speed limits ahead
note: Pentagonal signs warn drivers they are entering a school zone or near a school crossing.

question: Which color is commonly used for signs marking public recreation or cultural areas?
options: a:Brown,b:Red,c:Green
note: Brown signs are used to indicate public recreation and cultural points of interest.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
note: Stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the empty space and then back into the space while turning your wheel to maneuver in.

question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling,b:Activate your turn signal three to four seconds in advance,c:Increase your speed before turning
note: Signal several seconds before turning to inform other road users of your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal after changing lanes.,b:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.,c:Signal just before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Signal early enough to give other road users time to respond and avoid surprises when you pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,b:Changing lanes.,c:All of the above.
note: Always signal when changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking space or alley, or pulling into or out of parking spots.

question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:High beam headlights,c:Parking lights only
note: Use low beams in rainy or foggy conditions to reduce glare and improve visibility.

question: If you are involved in a crash, you should:
options: a:Leave the scene immediately to avoid trouble,b:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene and render aid as needed,c:Stand in traffic lanes to direct other drivers
note: Stop at or near the crash scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles, and avoid standing in traffic lanes.

question: You should sound your horn when you:
options: a:Are traveling through an intersection with a green light,b:See a child about to run into the street,c:Are passing a bicyclist in a residential area
note: Use your horn as a warning to prevent immediate danger, for example if a child runs into the street.

question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving in your lane,b:Pull to the right curb and stop,c:Slow down and continue
note: Immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.,b:Drive faster to get your mind off things.,c:Assume emotions won't affect your driving.
note: Strong emotions can distract you and reduce driving ability; wait until you feel focused and calm before driving.

question: Which factor directly affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The color of surrounding vehicles.,b:The number of passengers in other cars.,c:The condition of the road surface.
note: Stopping distance is greatly affected by road conditions (wet, icy, gravel), so reduce speed when roads are poor to maintain control.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a standard crossbuck and no gates or lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Turn down your radio to hear better and drive through quickly.,b:Cross immediately if you don’t see a train,c:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when sure no train is coming.,d:Speed up to clear the tracks faster.
note: At unprotected crossings you must look and listen for approaching trains from both directions and only cross when it is clearly safe.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Shift to neutral, apply the brakes as needed, carefully turn off the ignition to stop the engine, and move off the road to a safe location.,b:Brake hard and immediately open the hood while moving.,c:Keep driving until you reach a service station.
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral, apply steady braking, then turn off the engine (without locking the steering) and steer to a safe place to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at a green light but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection instead,b:Enter the intersection to prepare for the left turn if clear,c:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear
note: You may move into the intersection to prepare for a left turn on a green light if you won't block traffic, then complete the turn when safe.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: Do not brake hard; hold the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator to slow, steer straight, and pull off the road when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights to ask for a gap in traffic,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight,c:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left
note: Keep your wheels pointed straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign ahead, you should:
options: a:Try to drive around any lowered gates,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby,c:Speed up to cross before the train arrives
note: Warning signs indicate a possible train crossing; slow and be ready to stop. Never go around lowered gates.

question: When the traffic light turns from green to a solid yellow as you approach, you should:
options: a:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.,b:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,c:Speed up to beat the light.
note: A steady yellow warns that a red light is imminent; stop safely if you can, otherwise proceed through the intersection cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the freeway you see a \Merging traffic\" sign. You should:"
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over a lane if safe,b:Maintain your current speed regardless,c:Always honk at incoming traffic
note: Provide space for merging traffic by changing lanes or adjusting speed when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit or safe location to turn around,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder,c:Make the turn quickly from your current lane
note: Do not back up on the freeway; proceed to the next exit or suitable turnaround.

question: What should you do before driving in an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Plan your trip in advance,b:Rely solely on road signs to find your way,c:Only have a general idea of your destination
note: When going somewhere unfamiliar, prepare beforehand by checking maps or directions so you don't rely only on signs while driving.

question: During the first 180 days after receiving a probationary license, which restriction commonly applies?
options: a:May drive after midnight.,b:May not drive between 10:00 pm and 5:00 am.,c:May not transport immediate family members.
note: Probationary license holders face passenger and curfew restrictions, commonly not being allowed to drive between 10:00 pm and 5:00 am for the first 180 days.

question: What is the safe way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass,b:Honk to alert the bicyclist,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible
note: Give bicyclists plenty of room and reduce speed when passing; do not crowd or force them off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A green arrow pointing left.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A solid green light.
note: A green steady arrow allows you to proceed in the direction of the arrow with oncoming traffic required to stop for the turning movement.

question: What should drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They can stop faster than passenger vehicles,b:They need less space to turn than smaller cars,c:They have large blind spots and need more room to stop and maneuver
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and require greater distances to maneuver and stop than passenger vehicles.

question: When may you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights have stopped flashing,b:When the train has passed,c:Under no circumstances
note: Never drive around a lowered gate. Stop when warning signals, gates, or a flagger indicate an approaching train.

question: How can alcoholic beverages affect a driver?
options: a:They only affect very inexperienced drivers.,b:They improve coordination.,c:They can slow reaction time
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, coordination, and vision, increasing crash risk even at low levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed if clear,b:Stop only if pedestrians are present,c:Stop before entering the intersection
note: A red light requires a full stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or intersection and yielding to all vehicles and pedestrians with the right-of-way.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
note: On a downhill slope, turn your wheels toward the curb so a rolling vehicle will move away from traffic.

question: What should you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,b:Proceed through carefully after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, scanning for traffic from all directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over the others?
options: a:A steady red traffic light,b:A police officer directing traffic,c:A stop sign
note: Directions from a police officer or authorized traffic controller take precedence over signs and signals.

question: What is the only effective method to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee,b:Exercise,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol
note: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not lower BAC.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Whenever you see a bus regardless of lights,b:When the bus is stopped with red lights flashing and loading/unloading children,c:Only when the bus is parked on the shoulder
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights and/or extended stop arm while loading or unloading children.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn to warn kids.,b:Ignore it if there are no children visible.,c:Be alert for children and be prepared to stop.
note: Approach school crossings with caution; children may be present and can step into the road unexpectedly.

question: How can a person sober up quickly after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee will remove the effects of alcohol.,b:Drinking tomato juice and lime will sober them up.,c:Only the passage of time will reduce the effects of alcohol; coffee or fresh air will not sober you up.,d:Fresh air instantly cancels alcohol impairment.
note: No food, drink, or activity can speed removal of alcohol from the body; only time will reduce blood alcohol concentration.

question: How do blind spots of larger vehicles compare to smaller vehicles?
options: a:Larger vehicles have no blind spots,b:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots,c:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots
note: Bigger vehicles, like trucks, have larger blind spots especially close to their front, sides, and rear — avoid lingering there.

question: May you drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate,b:Only if an approaching train is not too close,c:You must never drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised
note: Do not go around or under moving crossing gates; wait until the gates are fully raised and signals have stopped.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, when should you allow a larger space cushion in front of you?
options: a:Never; keep the same spacing.,b:When stopped on an incline so the vehicle ahead cannot roll back into you.,c:Only at stop signs.,d:Only at traffic signals.
note: Allow extra space when stopped on a hill because the vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic starts moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do with your speed when making a turn?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control and stay in your lane,b:Increase your speed,c:Maintain your previous speed
note: When turning, slow to a speed that lets you maintain control, stay within your lane, and react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it not permitted to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When you want to pass a motorcycle.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:If doing so would interfere with traffic or be unsafe.,d:When the car ahead is disabled.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass only when it is safe and will not interfere with traffic; do not cross if it would create a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with two solid yellow centerlines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway,b:To pass if no oncoming traffic is visible,c:Never under any circumstances
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make left turns into or from private roads/driveways where permitted.

question: What do work zone signs indicate to drivers?
options: a:That it is summer,b:You must stop and back up immediately,c:Less-than-ideal driving conditions ahead
note: Work zone signs (orange) warn that road work is being done and drivers should be extra cautious.

question: When passing a large truck, a smaller vehicle should be prepared for:
options: a:Excess air pollution,b:Sudden wind gusts from the large vehicle,c:Loud noises
note: Large vehicles create air turbulence that can push smaller vehicles; be ready for corrective steering.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer vs. wine vs. liquor) change its effect on reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Wine impairs less than beer,b:Beer impairs less than wine,c:No — alcohol's effects depend on blood alcohol concentration
note: All alcoholic beverages impair reflexes and judgement depending on how much alcohol is consumed, not the specific beverage.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Certain prescription or over-the-counter medications.,c:A lack of sleep.,d:All of the above.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and fatigue; any of these can reduce judgment, reaction time, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Pedestrians in the roundabout only.,b:Bicyclists in the roundabout only.,c:Vehicles
note: Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians that are already in the roundabout before entering.

question: Why is driving at night generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark,c:It usually rains more at night.,d:Headlights are brighter at night.
note: Night driving reduces your field of vision and increases the risk of glare and encountering tired or impaired drivers; use appropriate headlights and reduce speed accordingly.

question: On a divided multilane highway, if you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,b:Slow down,c:Stop immediately in your travel lane.,d:Speed up to stay ahead.
note: Provide a clear path and stop as soon as safe so emergency responders can pass; do not attempt to outdrive the emergency vehicle.

question: Which is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than normal traffic only,b:Weaving between lanes,c:Making quick and sudden stops only
note: Signs of impairment include weaving, erratic lane changes, varying speeds, and jerky movements.

question: What is the 'No zone' with respect to large trucks and buses?
options: a:A speed-restricted zone.,b:A noise restriction area.,c:The large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from view.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots on all sides; avoid lingering in these areas where the driver cannot see you.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do immediately for safety?
options: a:Signal, exit the roadway carefully, use hazard flashers, and park where other drivers can see you.,b:Sit in the car and wait with the engine running.,c:Sound your horn to attract attention.,d:Stand behind your vehicle facing traffic.
note: Exit the lane safely, turn on hazards, move well off the road, and raise the hood to indicate your vehicle is disabled.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect on either,b:It harms both driving skills and judgement,c:It helps driving skills but harms judgement
note: Alcohol degrades reaction time, vision, coordination, and decision-making — harming both skills and judgment.

question: What is highway hypnosis and how does it occur?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
note: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare at the road for long periods and stop actively scanning, which can cause you to zone out and miss hazards.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect performance?
options: a:It has no effect on driving ability,b:It improves concentration so drivers make fewer errors,c:It increases the chance of driving errors and difficulty controlling the vehicle
note: Handling food or beverages distracts a driver’s hands and eyes, increasing the risk of lane drift and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstance may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is adequate room to pass.,b:When it requires driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a safe, available lane for passing; never pass off the pavement.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is:
options: a:Helpful to maintain driver alertness,b:A distracting activity,c:Not affecting driving abilities
note: Smoking can divert hands and eyes from driving and is a distracting activity that increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The right lane,b:Either lane as you choose,c:The lane closest to your previous lane
note: When turning onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane nearest to your original lane.

question: What does a posted advisory or speed restriction sign typically indicate?
options: a:Shows an advisory speed for curves and turns.,b:Is triangular in shape.,c:Is blue with black lettering.
note: Advisory speed signs show recommended safe speeds for curves and other conditions; reduce speed further in poor weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes?
options: a:You should always use cruise control.,b:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,c:Signal
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, signal and check mirrors and blind spots; use shoulder only for emergencies.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem indicate?
options: a:The vehicle must yield to all traffic.,b:The vehicle is designed to travel at 25 mph or slower and will display a reflective orange triangle.,c:The vehicle is a commercial vehicle.,d:The vehicle should be passed only on the left.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a highly reflective orange triangle and warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less.

question: Which is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter the curve and brake while exiting.,b:Slow down before entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.,c:Maintain a constant speed through the entire curve.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and gradually accelerate as you exit to maintain stability and control.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see in traffic.,b:They always break the law.,c:They must always yield to cars.
note: Smaller road users are harder to spot and may be less visible; stay alert to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A good rule to follow regarding passing other vehicles is:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary,b:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to see better,c:Pass on the right whenever possible
note: Passing increases collision risk, so drive with traffic speed limits and pass only when necessary and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if you find yourself stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stop to look up an address in the travel lane.,b:Drop off passengers in the travel lane.,c:Move out of the travel lane as soon as you can to a safe location; do not stop in a travel lane.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane; continue until you can safely pull off the roadway to the shoulder or a parking area.

question: If you are being tailgated, what should you do if you cannot change lanes?
options: a:Speed up aggressively to put distance between you.,b:Wait until the road ahead is clear and then reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Brake abruptly to warn the tailgater.,d:Honk continuously to make them back off.
note: If no right lane is available, gradually slow when safe to encourage the tailgater to pass; never brake suddenly as that increases collision risk.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas to slow and apply brakes smoothly,b:Always check mirrors and blind spots before stopping but stop abruptly when necessary,c:Tap your brakes repeatedly to warn the following driver
note: Gradually releasing the accelerator and applying steady braking reduces the likelihood of being hit from behind.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Yield only to vehicles from the left.,b:Continue normally without slowing.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.,d:Slow down and proceed with care.
note: A flashing yellow signal indicates caution; slow and proceed carefully when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what is required?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then turn when safe.,b:Maintain normal speed and turn without stopping.,c:Stop and look for police cars before turning.,d:Turn immediately without checking cross traffic.
note: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn on green but must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,c:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.
note: You must stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and not cross the sidewalk without stopping.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Pass with caution,b:Slow down immediately,c:Do not pass from your lane
note: A solid yellow line adjacent to your lane means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: To check your blind spot when moving left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: To ensure no vehicle is in your blind spot when changing lanes left, glance over your left shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Continue without changing speed.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop because the light will soon turn red.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is changing to red; slow down and stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
