options: a:Make a U-turn across the median.,b:Quickly cut across lanes to the exit.,c:Continue to the next exit and exit there rather than making a last-minute maneuver.
note: Do not make unsafe turns or U-turns on the interstate; proceed to the next exit and re-route from there.

question: Which of these does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:The condition of your brakes.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, braking distance, vehicle condition, speed, and road conditions — not time of day.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow the directions of the crossing guard,b:Ignore the guard and follow surrounding traffic,c:Assume the guard has no authority
note: Obey crossing guards and exercise extra caution in school zones, including reducing speed when directed.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Get off highways as quickly as possible,b:Reduce speed and increase following distance,c:Add extra weight to the vehicle for traction
note: Slowing down and increasing following distance are the most effective ways to reduce crash risk on snow or ice.

question: To prevent your physical condition from making you an unsafe driver, which of the following should you prioritize?
options: a:Drive within your physical limitations.,b:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,c:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.
note: Be aware of your physical limitations and only drive when fit; know how medications affect you and maintain health as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green arrow on a traffic signal allow you to do?
options: a:Should slow to a stop,b:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,c:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
note: A steady green arrow means you may make the indicated turn, but you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
options: a:Speed up to increase distance from them.,b:Slam on your brakes to warn them.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: Avoid conflict: let the tailgater pass by changing lanes or slowing slightly to increase the gap safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To whom must drivers yield?
options: a:Only pedestrians on the same side of the road.,b:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,c:Pedestrians only when they have a green signal.,d:Pedestrians in the roadway
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway at all times to avoid striking them, regardless of whether they are crossing carefully.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
options: a:Same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe,b:The traffic signal is broken and you may proceed without stopping,c:You do not have to stop completely
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop; then yield to traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate:
options: a:Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill,b:Passing is not allowed,c:Passing is allowed for drivers in both directions
note: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing for traffic in either direction.

question: Which of the following is true about railroad crossings?
options: a:Flaggers cannot direct vehicles at crossings.,b:It is illegal to go around lowered gates,c:All railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.,d:You may always go around lowered gates if traffic is light.
note: You must obey crossing devices and flaggers and never drive around lowered gates; additionally, many crossings lack active warning devices, so be cautious.

question: What does a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Directions to cities and towns,b:Traffic laws and regulations,c:A warning about conditions on or near the road ahead
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs with black symbols warn drivers of upcoming road conditions or hazards.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A speed limit sign.
note: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop, just like a stop sign; proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn, what should drivers do?
options: a:Signal in advance, watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and move into the left lane when appropriate.,b:Speed up and turn sharply.,c:Ignore pedestrians if you have the green.,d:Signal only after starting the turn.
note: Signal three to five seconds before turning, check mirrors, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and move into the left lane on multilane roads before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A single dashed yellow centerline means:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so,b:Drivers may not pass,c:Both lanes travel in the same direction
note: A dashed yellow centerline separates opposite-direction traffic and permits passing when it is safe.

question: Faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what is the safest course?
options: a:Try to split the difference and squeeze between both hazards.,b:Honk and speed up to get by quickly.,c:Pull onto the shoulder immediately.,d:Let the oncoming car pass
note: When two hazards exist, handle them sequentially by letting the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the bicyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What problem does driving much slower than the posted speed often create?
options: a:It guarantees you the right-of-way,b:You should never allow following cars to pass,c:It can be hazardous and may require you to pull off to let traffic pass
note: Driving significantly slower than traffic flow can be dangerous; on two-lane roads you must pull over if you are impeding traffic.

question: What danger can a leaking exhaust system pose to occupants?
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning that can cause drowsiness or death,b:Excessive oil consumption,c:Need for more frequent tune-ups
note: A leaky exhaust can allow toxic fumes, including carbon monoxide, into the cabin, potentially causing drowsiness, unconsciousness, or death.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, what should you do after a train passes?
options: a:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.,b:Immediately go through once the first train passes.,c:Cross quickly without checking other tracks.
note: When there are multiple tracks, a train passing on one track does not mean the crossing is clear; check all tracks before crossing.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Stop on the edge of the road and re-enter quickly.,b:Slow down without braking sharply,c:Accelerate to regain control.,d:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
note: Reduce speed gently and when safe steer back onto the pavement carefully; avoid hard braking or jerky steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, after you stop you should look which directions before proceeding?
options: a:Right first,b:Only check behind you for tailgating vehicles,c:Left first
note: When stopped, look left (nearest traffic), then right, then left again before proceeding to ensure safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, how should you indicate turns?
options: a:Use hand signals,b:Use your headlights,c:Use your horn
note: Use standardized hand signals to indicate turning or stopping when turn signals are inoperative.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, how should you yield on a two-lane road?
options: a:Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass.,b:Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass.,c:Drive as far toward the right side of the road as is safe and stop.
note: On two-lane roads you must pull as far right as possible and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: Which actions can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Only talking on the phone,b:Only changing the radio station,c:Eating
note: Many common activities—eating, using a phone, adjusting devices—distract drivers and reduce safety.

question: To help prevent collisions, you should:
options: a:Communicate with other road users by signaling and using warnings,b:Ignore other drivers on the road,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads
note: Communicate intentions—use turn signals, horn, or lights—to make your actions predictable and reduce crashes.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead, you should:
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake,b:Stare straight ahead at all times,c:Continuously scan the entire roadway and roadside
note: Scan far ahead as well as the sides of the road to identify potential hazards early.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way,b:Call the other driver names out the window,c:Flash your lights to show them they're wrong
note: Avoid escalation: stay calm, slow down or change lanes, and let the aggressive driver go on.

question: What do working brake lights signal to drivers behind you?
options: a:Are changing lanes.,b:Are slowing down or stopping.,c:Are making a turn.
note: Brake lights indicate to other drivers that you are slowing or stopping; they must be kept in working order.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.,b:Follow the flagger's directions.,c:Assume the flagger is mistaken.
note: Flaggers control traffic for safety in work zones; you must obey their signals and directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,b:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,c:Must slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light allows you to proceed through the intersection when it is safe; turns are permitted unless prohibited but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk when using which device?
options: a:CD player,b:Radio,c:Cell phone
note: Cell phone use, including hands-free devices, significantly increases crash risk; any activity that diverts attention is dangerous.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding vehicle lights?
options: a:Use only parking lights,b:Use four-way flashers exclusively,c:Turn on your headlights (use low beams near other vehicles)
note: Turn on headlights at dusk or when visibility is reduced; dim to low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet when following.

question: How does even a small amount of alcohol affect driving abilities?
options: a:Alcohol does not limit those abilities.,b:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can limit those abilities.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can limit your concentration
note: Any amount of alcohol reduces concentration, perception, judgment, and memory; no amount is safe if you intend to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic while the traffic light is working, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to get the officer's attention.,b:Obey only the traffic light.,c:Follow the officer's directions.
note: An officer's directions override traffic signals, and drivers must follow the officer's signals and instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Pass only on the right.,b:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, ensure the lane you will use to pass is clear and signal your lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Drivers may choose to ignore the arrow if no other traffic is present,b:Drivers must stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow,c:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow
note: Lane arrows require drivers in the marked lane to follow the indicated movement, subject to traffic signals and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on which side must yield?
options: a:The car on the left shall yield to the car on the right,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way,c:The larger vehicle must yield
note: At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:Railroad crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean no passing by traffic in either direction except for specific permitted turns.

question: If another vehicle seems likely to hit you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Use your emergency lights.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they may not see you and a collision is possible.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of injury in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways,b:Wear your seat belt,c:Limit your driving to weekdays
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce death and serious injury in a crash.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes?
options: a:Force the bicyclist off the road.,b:Slow down,c:Honk and pass closely to quickly clear the rider.
note: Pass bicyclists with caution, allowing at least 3 feet of clearance (more at higher speeds) and only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'No stopping' sign generally allow you to do?
options: a:Stop only to avoid conflict with traffic or to obey a police officer or traffic signal,b:Stop briefly to unload packages,c:Stop to discharge passengers whenever you choose
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may only stop to obey traffic officials or signals or to avoid a traffic conflict — not for loading or unloading.

question: If borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Assume it functions like your usual car and drive away,b:Familiarize yourself with controls (signals,c:Hide any defects to avoid embarrassment
note: Take time to locate and test important controls and correct any defects before driving an unfamiliar vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a steady yellow arrow, how should drivers respond?
options: a:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is coming; stop unless you are already in the intersection and it is unsafe to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite-direction traffic, you should:
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left shortly,b:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately after passing,c:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle
note: After passing, move back into your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate as quickly as possible,b:Reverse slowly,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians still in the intersection
note: A green light means you may go, but you must first yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.

question: On slippery roads, which driving adjustment should you make?
options: a:Maintain the same gap as in normal conditions.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive as you would on dry roads.
note: Slippery conditions increase stopping distance, so increase the gap between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump your brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: If your car lacks ABS, pumping the brakes helps you stop quickly while retaining some steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yield sign at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Yield only to traffic on your left.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Always come to a full stop regardless of conditions.
note: A yield sign means slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in the road you plan to enter.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.,b:Let it go.,c:Flash your high beams at the driver.
note: To avoid road rage and unsafe behavior, remain calm and continue driving safely rather than retaliating.

question: Which of the following are effects of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:Loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment.,b:Increase in reaction speed.,c:Improved night vision.,d:Greater alertness.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination, all of which reduce driving safety.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White,b:Yellow and white,c:Yellow
note: Yellow pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street, where should you begin the turn?
options: a:From the right lane.,b:From the center of the intersection.,c:From the left lane.
note: To turn left from a multilane one-way street, start the turn from the leftmost lane unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: Why is keeping a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.,b:Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
note: A space cushion gives you time and room to react to other drivers' mistakes and to avoid hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you permitted to pass another vehicle?
options: a:By using the highway shoulder when traffic is slow,b:On hills and curves if you think no oncoming car is near,c:Only where it is legal and safe — never on a hill
note: Passing on hills, curves, intersections, or by using the shoulder is unsafe and commonly illegal; pass only where allowed and safe.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or not permitted.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes going the same direction and generally mean lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle,b:Only behind your vehicle,c:Only on the left and right sides
note: Maintain space on all sides of your vehicle to allow time and room to react to hazards.

question: What are signs that require drivers to obey an instruction called?
options: a:Information signs,b:Warning signs,c:Regulatory signs
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of laws and requirements; failure to obey can result in penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way road, you may not pass from either direction when the centerline is:
options: a:Single broken yellow,b:Double solid yellow,c:Combination solid and broken yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means no passing from either direction.

question: What should a driver do when taking a non-prescription drug before driving?
options: a:Drink alcohol instead to counteract effects,b:Assume no effect and drive normally,c:Read the drug label for warnings about driving
note: Many over-the-counter meds can impair driving. Read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure about effects on driving.

question: If your car begins to skid, which direction should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:Toward the nearest curb regardless of skid direction.,b:Sharp opposite the skid.,c:To keep the front wheels straight.,d:In the direction you want the vehicle to go (into the skid).
note: Turn the wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go; as traction returns, straighten the wheel to regain control.

question: Which practice helps most to prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive through standing water as quickly as possible.,b:Keep cruise control on in wet weather.,c:Reduce speed when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.
note: Lower speeds and properly maintained tires (tread and pressure) greatly reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What is the correct sequence before changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.,b:Check mirrors and immediately change lanes.,c:Signal and change lanes without checking, d:Check your blind spot only after you start changing lanes.
note: Activate your signal, check rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check the blind spot, then change when safe.

question: Where is it unlawful to park?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes is illegal; when parking on a street you must be within 12 inches of the curb.

question: What is the typical meaning of orange-colored traffic signs?
options: a:Regulatory instructions.,b:School zone warnings.,c:Work zone warnings.
note: Orange signs indicate construction, maintenance, or emergency work zones and warn drivers to use caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When entering a highway with other cars present,b:When anything makes conditions less than perfect (wet roads,c:Only if you see a police car
note: Drive slower than the posted limit when conditions—weather, visibility, road surface—warrant reduced speed for safety.

question: From a center left-turn lane, which maneuvers are permitted?
options: a:Use the lane to pass slow-moving traffic.,b:Use it to make U-turns only.,c:Drive through the lane as through-traffic.,d:Make left turns from the lane when indicated.
note: A center left-turn lane is reserved for left turns; it should not be used for passing or as a through lane.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Immediately accelerate and swerve back onto the road.,b:Gently ease off the accelerator,c:Stop immediately and get out of the vehicle.
note: If your right wheels run off the pavement, remain calm, slow down by easing off the gas, steer parallel to the roadway, and return to the pavement when it is safe to do so.

question: Which statement correctly describes alcohol’s effect on driving?
options: a:Alcohol increases coordination.,b:Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction times.,c:Alcohol will make you more alert.,d:Alcohol improves night vision.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and reduces the abilities needed for safe driving, such as reaction time and judgment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a required practice when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,b:When passing,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes.
note: When passing, use your mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots; wait until you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview before returning.

question: At a light rail intersection, what must you always do?
options: a:Ignore signals if no train is visible.,b:Drive around lowered gates if traffic is heavy.,c:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all traffic signals and signs.,d:Assume trains will yield to your vehicle.
note: Treat rail intersections with caution: obey signals, do not drive around lowered gates, and check both directions before crossing.

question: What can happen if alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be reduced.
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can intensify the effects of both, producing greater impairment than either alone.

question: A \No standing\" sign means you may:"
options: a:Never stop your vehicle there,b:Park there if the driver remains in the vehicle,c:Stop only temporarily to load or unload passengers
note: \No standing\" prohibits parking; you may only make a brief stop to pick up or drop off passengers."

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, what is the safest action?
options: a:Lay down in the car and sleep,b:Stay in your car and wait for help,c:Get out and walk for help immediately
note: Remain in your vehicle to be more likely to be found; run the engine periodically for heat while ensuring the exhaust pipe is clear.

question: Driving without the required liability insurance is:
options: a:Not illegal but not recommended,b:Against the law,c:Without legal repercussions
note: Indiana law requires drivers to carry minimum liability insurance (commonly 25/50/25 limits); driving without it is illegal.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice before entering a roadway or crosswalk?
options: a:Enter at any time because drivers must stop for you,b:Always insist on your right-of-way over vehicles,c:Do not enter when vehicles are approaching; wait until it is safe to cross
note: Even when pedestrians have the right-of-way, do not step into traffic if vehicles are too close to stop safely; wait until it is safe.

question: How should you behave when approaching an accident scene?
options: a:Park and approach the accident to observe,b:Keep your attention on driving and keep moving unless you are involved or emergency help hasn't arrived,c:Stop to look at the scene
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; remain alert and continue safely past the area.

question: How would you characterize distracted driving?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers drivers, passengers, and others.,b:Very uncommon and not a major concern.,c:Harmless if only for a few seconds.,d:Required for multitasking drivers.
note: Distracted driving significantly increases crash risk; staying focused on driving and scanning the road is essential for safety.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait and only move it after police arrive.,b:Drive away immediately to avoid a traffic jam.,c:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,d:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: After a minor collision, move vehicles out of the flow of traffic if you can do so safely, while still identifying yourself and rendering assistance as required by law.

question: What must you confirm before passing another vehicle?
options: a:That you can roughly apply the brakes if needed.,b:That you can cross over a solid lane marking.,c:That the passing lane is clear,d:That the other driver is signaling to let you pass.
note: Safe passing requires checking traffic ahead and in adjacent lanes, checking mirrors and blind spots, and ensuring passing is legal and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:Only at railroad crossings,b:On hills and curves,c:Only at intersections
note: Passing is unsafe and often illegal on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings; these are common no-pass locations.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:Always safe if you use high beams.,c:No different in risk.,d:More dangerous because visibility is reduced and hazards are harder to see.
note: Night driving reduces visibility and increases risks from glare and fatigued or impaired drivers; slow down and use appropriate lighting.

question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass before they reach your lane.,b:Flash your lights and continue slowly.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way.
note: Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and be prepared to come to a full stop when they are crossing in your path.

question: What should you do when driving on major highways to avoid fatigue or inattention?
options: a:Rely on cruise control to manage speed,b:Maintain a steady gaze straight ahead to concentrate,c:Stay alert
note: To avoid 'highway hypnosis,' keep scanning the road, remain alert, and be prepared to respond to hazards.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Only honk at other drivers.,b:Only adjust the radio.,c:Take your eyes off the road,d:Only use cruise control.
note: Distracting activities that remove your eyes, hands, or attention from driving increase crash risk; avoid multitasking while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front,b:Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic moves,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking intersections is illegal and dangerous.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to crashes?
options: a:Following too closely,b:Excessive speed for conditions,c:Inattentive driving
note: All listed factors—distracted driving, driving too fast for conditions, and tailgating—commonly cause crashes.

question: If a solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, what does that indicate?
options: a:Construction zone ends.,b:The road narrows ahead.,c:You must turn left soon.,d:There is an intersection ahead.
note: An edge line angling toward the center means the road narrows; the edge line marks the boundary between travel lane and shoulder.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:It is acceptable to follow motorcycles closely,b:A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than one with one rider,c:You must change lanes completely when you pass a motorcycle
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; you should move fully into the left lane before passing one on the left.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights or sounding a siren, you must:
options: a:Yield and immediately pull to the right curb and stop,b:Continue driving in your lane,c:Slow down and keep moving
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, you must pull over to the side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way do you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so a rolling vehicle will move away from traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid red arrow shown by a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the arrow's direction,b:The same as a circular red light — you must stop and may not turn in that direction,c:The arrow is not used in traffic signals
note: A solid red arrow means traffic in that lane must stop and may not proceed in the arrow's direction.

question: Which area is your vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:Directly behind your vehicle,b:You see it in your rearview mirror,c:An area you cannot see without moving your head
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head; they are usually to the sides and rear of your vehicle.

question: If another driver is trying to pass your vehicle, how should you assist them?
options: a:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,c:Pull off the road.
note: Maintain your lane and adjust speed as needed to help the passing vehicle merge back safely; do not pull off the road into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a multi-lane street moving in your direction, where should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, enter the lane closest to the lane you used to turn. Do not change lanes immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you pull over and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle with lights?
options: a:Always pull to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of the emergency vehicle's direction,b:Only if it is following you,c:Only if it is coming from the opposite direction
note: Pull to the right and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens whether they are approaching from front or behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver with left arm and hand extended upward is signaling they plan to:
options: a:Come to a stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Turn left.,d:Slow down.
note: A left arm extended upward indicates an intention to turn right using hand signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver signaling with left arm and hand extended downward is indicating they intend to:
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Merge right.,d:Stop or slow down.
note: A left arm extended downward is the hand signal for slowing or stopping; watch and adjust your driving accordingly.

question: When driving in general traffic, what is the safest practice regarding speed?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to get ahead.,b:Drive slower than everyone else.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits rather than much faster or slower.,d:Constantly fluctuate your speed to stay alert.
note: Crashes often occur when drivers travel much faster or slower than surrounding traffic; maintain a speed consistent with the flow and legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, it is usually best to:
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and then enter traffic.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely merged.,d:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and merge when a gap appears.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway traffic speed and merge safely; yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,b:Turn the wheel sharply away from the skid.,c:Brake hard and keep the wheel straight.,d:Turn into oncoming traffic.
note: When skidding, remain calm and steer in the direction of the skid so the vehicle can regain traction and straighten out.

question: How can the risk of hydroplaning be reduced while driving in wet conditions?
options: a:By driving through deeper water rather than shallower.,b:By driving more slowly.,c:By accelerating through standing water.
note: Driving at lower speeds in wet conditions reduces the chance that tires will lose contact with the road surface.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or fall back until the other driver can see you,b:Maintain your current speed and position,c:Stay in the blind spot to avoid merging confusion
note: Do not linger in someone else's blind spot; adjust speed to move where the driver can see you.

question: How can you avoid collisions caused by blind spots?
options: a:Honk before every lane change,b:Adjust your rearview mirror frequently while moving,c:Turn your head quickly to check the blind spot before changing lanes
note: Before turning or changing lanes, glance over your shoulder to confirm your blind spot is clear; don't rely solely on mirrors.

question: Which headlights should you use in foggy weather?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Hazard lights only.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if available) in fog; high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean when displayed for turn control?
options: a:It is never used as a traffic signal,b:Slow down and prepare for the arrow to change to red (same as a circular yellow),c:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated without yielding
note: A solid yellow arrow functions like a circular yellow light: it warns the protected-turn signal is ending and you must prepare to stop.

question: Which statement best describes how to respond to sudden changes in weather while driving?
options: a:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,b:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,c:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
note: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving (speed, following distance, and attention) to match the conditions.

question: Which safety restraints are most effective in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap and shoulder belt,b:Only an airbag,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag used together
note: Seat belts combined with airbags provide the best protection; airbags are supplemental and effective when belts are worn.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you lose control or need to warn another road user of imminent danger.,b:To express frustration when someone cuts you off.,c:To greet friends driving nearby.,d:Constantly while passing bicyclists.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of danger; do not use it for anger or greeting purposes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn others.,b:Swing to the right side of your lane to make the turn easier.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: When changing lanes, what is the correct signaling practice?
options: a:Begin signaling while you are moving into the lane,b:Rely exclusively on mirrors without signaling,c:Signal in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas or 5 seconds on freeways) and not as you move into the lane
note: Signal well before the maneuver, check mirrors and blind spots, then change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to stop as if at a stop sign?
options: a:Yellow arrow.,b:Steady yellow light.,c:Flashing red light.
note: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, check for traffic, and proceed when clear.

question: Regulatory signs are usually which color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Green,b:White,c:Blue
note: Regulatory signs are typically white with black markings and control traffic movement; they must be obeyed.

question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to give the vehicle space; if you cannot change lanes, slow down and pass cautiously.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Continue at the same speed in your lane.
note: Move over a lane if it is safe; otherwise slow down below the posted limit and pass carefully to provide room for responders.

question: What is the unique shape used for stop signs?
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Octagon.,c:Circle.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign is used only for stop signs, signaling drivers to come to a complete stop.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,b:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,c:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child
note: Always ensure all occupants are properly restrained; infants should ride in the rear and never in a rear-facing seat where a front airbag is active.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph take to stop?
options: a:Almost 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.,d:About 200 feet.
note: Large trucks require much longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles; a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph may need nearly 400 feet to stop.

question: When you notice other drivers acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact.,b:Distance yourself from the situation.,c:Don't react with hand gestures.
note: Avoid escalating the situation: keep your distance, avoid eye contact and gestures, and make maneuvers to remove yourself from harm.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit sign indicates:
options: a:Only a suggested speed.,b:The exact safe speed for all conditions.,c:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions for that roadway.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions are poor.

question: Which of these is NOT a factor in determining the distance it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Reaction distance.,b:Braking distance.,c:Steering ability.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a stopping-distance component.

question: What does a dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and you may change lanes when safe.,b:Traffic is moving in opposite directions.,c:You may not pass.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes traveling the same way and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor that affects blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,c:How much you drink.,d:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC is affected by the amount consumed, body weight, and time between drinks; the type of beverage does not determine BAC.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do when one train passes?
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
note: After one train passes, check for trains on the adjacent track; do not cross until you are sure no other train is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping,b:The driver on the left,c:The driver on the right
note: When two drivers arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on the right and proceed when safe.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what is the best action to take?
options: a:Stop driving.,b:Open your window.,c:Get some coffee.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similarly to alcohol; the safest option is to stop driving and rest.

question: Which is true about work zones?
options: a:They may be stationary or moving and require extra caution.,b:They are marked with black and white signs.,c:You do not need to slow down.
note: Work zones can be fixed or mobile; they are typically marked with orange signs and require reduced speed and heightened attention.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, remember they generally:
options: a:Require longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles,b:Require less distance to stop than smaller vehicles,c:Have a smaller turning radius than cars
note: Because of their mass, trucks need greater distances to slow and stop; allow extra space and avoid their blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, who must yield?
options: a:The merging driver may force their way into traffic.,b:No one needs to yield if traffic is light.,c:The driver entering the interstate should yield to vehicles already on it.,d:Drivers on the interstate must always yield to merging vehicles.
note: Drivers on acceleration ramps should yield to traffic already on the interstate and merge when a safe gap appears.

question: On average, your body eliminates alcohol at about what rate?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks an hour,b:One alcoholic drink an hour,c:Two alcoholic drinks an hour
note: On average the body metabolizes approximately one standard drink per hour, though individual rates vary.

question: What are the typical colors for warning signs that alert drivers to upcoming hazards?
options: a:White symbols on blue,b:Black symbols on a white background,c:Black symbols on a yellow background
note: Warning signs generally use a yellow background with black symbols; work zone warnings use orange with black symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle,b:Honk your horn loudly,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes
note: Only pass when safe: check mirrors, check blind spots, signal, then complete the pass and return when you can see the passed vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming driver is headed into your lane, what should you do first?
options: a:Sound your horn, steer right, and brake to reduce impact.,b:Steer left and accelerate.,c:Brake and swerve left without warning.,d:Flash your lights and keep your speed.
note: Honk to attract attention, attempt to escape to the right if possible, and brake firmly; every mph you slow before impact reduces severity.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should pedestrians walk on?
options: a:The side with the lightest traffic.,b:The side facing oncoming traffic.,c:The same side as traffic is moving.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and react if necessary.

question: When roads may be slippery, you should:
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed,b:Reduce your following distance,c:Always drive at the maximum posted speed
note: On slippery roads reduce speed and increase your following distance; avoid using cruise control.

question: You approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. Under which condition must you stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If the crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.,d:All of the above.
note: You must stop before crossing when a stop sign is present, a gate is lowered, flashing red lights are activated, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or so close that crossing would be hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a traffic signal showing a green arrow with a red light allow you to do?
options: a:You may only drive straight ahead.,b:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,c:You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
note: A green arrow with a red light permits movement only in the arrow's direction, and only when the intersection is clear.

question: When sleet or snow begins, what should you do while driving?
options: a:Turn off headlights to reduce glare.,b:Allow extra following distance and keep windshield and mirrors clear.,c:Drive at the posted speed to keep traffic flowing.
note: Snow and sleet increase stopping distances; clear visibility and additional following space are essential.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Drive out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching cars,c:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway
note: Yield to both pedestrians and vehicles on the main roadway when entering from a private road or driveway.

question: Which actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Try to get to your destination as fast as possible.,b:Flash headlights repeatedly.,c:Allow extra travel time,d:Tailgate slower drivers to encourage them to move.
note: Planning ahead, following traffic laws, and signaling properly reduce stress and the likelihood of aggressive encounters.

question: Where on the roadway do sections tend to freeze first and stay icy longest?
options: a:Areas shaded by trees or buildings,b:Flat sections of road,c:Curvy sections of road
note: Shaded areas freeze and retain ice or moisture longer, so they require extra caution in cold or wet weather.

question: What effect does drinking coffee have on blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:It cancels the effects of alcohol.,b:It has no effect on BAC; only time reduces BAC.,c:It increases BAC temporarily.,d:It decreases BAC quickly.
note: Coffee may make you feel more awake but it does not lower the alcohol in your bloodstream; only time does.

question: What are the risks associated with worn or bald tires?
options: a:Can make turning more difficult.,b:Are likely to hydroplane.,c:Can increase your stopping distance.
note: Tires with little tread increase the chance of hydroplaning, reduce traction for turning, and lengthen stopping distances.

question: On which surfaces does your vehicle require a greater stopping distance?
options: a:On a wet or icy road.,b:On paved highways.,c:When driving at night.
note: Wet, icy, or loose surfaces increase stopping distance; always increase following distance in these conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions.,b:The maximum posted speed only.,c:A speed that is safe for the conditions only.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the area and conditions, even if the posted speed is higher.

question: If you must drive in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights to see farther.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: Low beams and fog lights improve visibility in foggy conditions; high beams create glare and reduce vision.

question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Prescription medications, over-the-counter remedies, illegal drugs, and some cold/allergy medicines.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only marijuana.,d:Caffeine only.
note: Many substances—legal and illegal—can impair driving ability; always check side effects and avoid driving when impaired.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates what?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: When a broken yellow line is alongside a solid yellow line, traffic next to the broken line may pass when safe; traffic next to the solid line may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign with no marked stop line or crosswalk, you may proceed after:
options: a:Slowing and verifying no cross traffic,b:Coming to a complete stop and verifying it is safe to proceed,c:Stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line beside your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:You may pass when traffic is clear and it is safe to do so.,c:Never.,d:Only during daytime hours.
note: If the broken line is next to your lane you may cross it to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to pass.

question: Why should you avoid following other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly,b:You may miss the vehicle's turn signals,c:You may not see the road between the cars
note: Following too closely reduces the time available to stop or react, increasing the chance of a rear-end collision.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Ignore the tracks if you don't see a train.,b:Drive around a lowered gate if traffic is light.,c:Look,d:Try to speed up to beat a train.
note: Always look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop for any crossing, regardless of whether signals are present.

question: How should you pass an animal you encounter on the roadway?
options: a:The driver should honk their horn.,b:Pass the animal as closely as possible.,c:Pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.
note: Approach and pass animals slowly and cautiously to avoid frightening them and causing an unpredictable reaction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop even if clear,b:Slow down,c:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking
note: At intersections without signs or signals, slow down, check all directions, and yield as necessary to avoid a crash.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels,c:Toward the right side of the road
note: Glance to the right edge of the road to avoid being temporarily blinded by another vehicle's high beams while keeping enough sight of the roadway to stay on course.

question: If you drink alcohol socially, which action best helps ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Take a cold shower before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Drink coffee before driving.
note: Arranging a sober ride prevents driving while impaired; coffee or showers do not reduce blood alcohol concentration.

question: Which of the following substances can impair driving and lead to a DUII?
options: a:Only inhalants,b:Only beer and wine,c:Only illegal drugs,d:Alcohol
note: Many substances can impair driving, including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and prescription or over-the-counter medications.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look only into the rearview mirror.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Look only into the side mirror.,d:Glance over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter.
note: Before changing lanes you should look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to confirm no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Driving while distracted by an activity usually has what effect on a driver?
options: a:Usually causes the driver to drive faster.,b:Is never dangerous.,c:Usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.
note: Distractions reduce a driver's ability to perceive and react to hazards, increasing crash risk.

question: At night, which is hardest to see?
options: a:Other motorists,b:Pedestrians,c:Road signs
note: Pedestrians are the most difficult to see at night compared to signs or other vehicles.

question: If the driver ahead is inattentive and talking to a passenger, what should you do?
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space because their safety margin is reduced.,b:Follow closely to monitor their behavior.,c:Signal them to drive faster.,d:Honk repeatedly to draw attention.
note: Allow additional space for distracted drivers because their increased likelihood of errors raises the risk of collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in line at a stop sign and cross traffic clears, what must you do?
options: a:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding,b:Proceed without stopping because you already stopped once,c:Roll slowly through the sign without stopping
note: You must come to a complete stop at the stop sign or line each time before proceeding when safe.

question: When it begins to rain and visibility drops, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the rain faster.,b:Slow down and turn on your headlights to be seen by other drivers.,c:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless.
note: Reduce speed, use headlights, and if visibility becomes too poor, pull off the road safely until conditions improve.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which of the following is important?
options: a:Ensure the target lane is clear before moving into it.,b:Ignore your blind spot if mirrors look clear.,c:Change lanes without signaling to be quick.
note: Always signal in advance, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear before changing lanes.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the center line.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Either side equally.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while still keeping enough view to maintain your lane position.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which steady light will soon appear?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing red.
note: A steady yellow means the light is about to change to steady red; be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass other cars when in a hurry,b:To turn left into or from a driveway or private road (or make permitted U-turns),c:To pass a slow-moving truck
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit lane changes and passing except to make permitted left turns into or from driveways or intersections.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:
options: a:Directed to do so by a flagger,b:There is a stop sign controlling the crossing,c:Flashing red signals and crossing gates are operating
note: Stop when warnings are active (flashing lights, lowered gates) or when directed by signs or flaggers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, how should you usually merge?
options: a:Stop first then creep into traffic.,b:Use your horn continuously while merging.,c:Enter well below traffic speed and force others to slow.,d:Signal
note: Use acceleration lanes to reach the speed of traffic, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap; yield to mainline traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and hold your lane.,b:Slow down to create space in front for the other vehicle to pass safely.,c:Speed up to get away.
note: If someone wants to pass, slow down slightly to give them room to complete the pass more quickly and safely.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign usually indicates:
options: a:Road hazard or warning sign,b:An interstate route sign,c:School crossing sign
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert drivers to hazardous locations or special driving conditions ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow centerline, what does that tell you?
options: a:You are entering a two-way road where passing is permitted when safe,b:You are on a one-way road,c:The road is under repair
note: A broken yellow line separates two-way traffic and may be crossed to pass when conditions are safe.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Cross at your own risk if no signals are active.,b:Honk and proceed.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,d:Slow and then cross quickly.
note: If a train is near enough to be a danger, do not attempt to cross even if no signals are working; wait until it is completely clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a flashing red traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign — come to a full stop and proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping,c:Continue through if there is no crossing traffic
note: A flashing red traffic signal must be treated the same as a stop sign: stop completely, then continue only when safe.

question: How should a lap belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Hidden under the seat,b:Loose across your stomach,c:Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen
note: Lap belts should be snug across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should rest comfortably across the chest.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line separating lanes is which of the following?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.,d:Solid white line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe; double solid or solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:The parked car will remain stationary,b:The driver may open their door into your path,c:The driver will signal before opening the door.
note: Assume doors may open and children may appear; slow down and leave extra space when passing parked vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it required to signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb?
options: a:Yes — signaling is required by law and is a good driving habit.,b:Only if other traffic is present.,c:Not necessary if you think it is obvious.
note: You must signal your intentions in advance (at least 100 feet on most roads) to inform other drivers of your planned move.

question: What is a \No zone\" for large vehicles?"
options: a:A designated no-passing area,b:A one-way traffic area,c:The large blind spots alongside and behind a truck or bus
note: \No zones\" are the large blind spots around trucks where smaller vehicles should avoid lingering."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what sequence of checks should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles without checking mirrors.,b:Check both side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,c:Check your side view mirror only.
note: Check side and rearview mirrors for approaching traffic and then glance over your shoulder to verify your blind spot before moving lanes.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching another vehicle; low beams provide safe visibility without blinding others.

question: On slippery roads, how should you adjust your driving?
options: a:Slow down and drive more slowly than the posted speed if conditions require.,b:Drive faster to get through slippery areas quickly.,c:Maintain the posted speed exactly at all times.,d:Turn off traction control immediately.
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of slippery conditions like rain or ice and increase following distance; sometimes driving below the posted limit is safest.

question: When may you legally cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:During daylight hours only.,b:Any time there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Only to turn into or out of a driveway
note: Solid yellow centerlines generally prohibit passing; you may cross them to turn into or out of driveways, businesses, or other legal turns.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Maintain good tread depth, proper tire inflation, and reduce speed in rain,b:Only ensure tires are properly inflated,c:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed
note: Prevent hydroplaning by ensuring tires have adequate tread and inflation and by slowing down in wet conditions.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,c:Slow down until it passes you.
note: Yield the right-of-way by pulling as far right as safely possible and stopping until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It improves reaction time.,b:It causes you to always drive more carefully.,c:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and focus on driving tasks.
note: Stress can distract you, reduce concentration, and impair decision-making — delay driving until you can focus.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service station.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Brake hard immediately to stop as quickly as possible.
note: Keep the vehicle straight, ease off the accelerator, avoid heavy braking until you have control, then pull over to a safe place.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you allow?
options: a:Give the motorcycle the full lane; a motorcycle is entitled to the entire lane.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,c:Allow the motorcycle only half a lane.,d:Require the motorcyclist to ride in the center of the lane.
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle and needs the full width of a lane to maneuver safely; do not crowd or share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: After a school bus finishes unloading and its stop arm is withdrawn, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed immediately once the bus moves,b:Wait until the children wave at you,c:Watch for children walking near the roadway before proceeding
note: After a bus stops unloading, be alert for children who may be near or crossing the road before you proceed.

question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Proceed but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Stop and check all directions.,c:Treat it like a yield sign.
note: A steady green means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.

question: What is the primary cause recorded in over 93% of fatal collisions?
options: a:Malfunctioning traffic signals.,b:Unsafe road conditions exclusively.,c:Weather alone.,d:Driver action or error.
note: Most fatal crashes are primarily caused by driver actions or failures to observe traffic laws, such as inattention or poor decision-making.

question: How should you safely cross a railroad track?
options: a:Only cross when the red light is flashing.,b:Rely solely on your vehicle's radio to detect trains.,c:Listen and look both ways,d:Cross rapidly when you hear a distant train.
note: Always look and listen for trains before crossing, obey signals, and never proceed until you are certain the tracks are clear.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers who:
options: a:Consistently check their mirrors and blind spots,b:Yield the right-of-way frequently,c:Drive too fast for conditions
note: Driving too fast for road or weather conditions is a common cause of crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an intersection controlled by signs at the same time, which driver must yield?
options: a:Either driver at random.,b:The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.,c:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

question: Which statement about driving on a wet roadway is true?
options: a:Water does not affect cars with good tires,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water,c:As you drive faster
note: Higher speeds reduce tire contact with the road and increase hydroplaning risk; slow down on wet surfaces.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn loudly and back out slowly.,b:Rely only on mirrors and cameras.,c:Get out and walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: When small children are nearby, exit the vehicle and visually check behind it before backing to avoid accidents.

question: Which actions help reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Avoid speeding on wet roads.,b:Ignore tire tread condition.,c:Drive faster through puddles.
note: Reducing speed on wet roads, maintaining proper tire pressure, and replacing tires with poor tread all lower hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red light, you should:
options: a:Honk to warn the pedestrians,b:Speed up past the pedestrians,c:Stop and allow pedestrians to cross safely
note: Yield to pedestrians even if you have a green light; they must be allowed to cross safely.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass, and the bicyclist may swerve into traffic,b:Bicycles always have the right-of-way,c:You are moving slower than a bicycle
note: Bicyclists can swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming traffic may not notice your movement, so pass with care and give ample space.

question: Which actions help you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Not drive if you are tired.,b:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, ensure headlights work, and avoid driving if fatigued for safety.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert to motorcycles on the road?
options: a:Motorcycles must always ride on the shoulder.,b:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.,c:Motorcycles never use headlights.,d:Motorcyclists are always less skilled than car drivers.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss in traffic and more difficult to judge for speed and distance; give them extra caution and space.

question: On slick roads you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly to avoid slipping,b:Change lanes quickly,c:Take turns more slowly than usual
note: Approach turns and curves more slowly on slippery surfaces to maintain traction and control.

question: Which driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in your driveway with the engine running,b:Slowing down gradually and anticipating stops,c:Accelerating quickly from stops
note: Gradually adjusting speed and avoiding unnecessary braking and acceleration saves fuel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection with blocked views, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane clears,b:Proceed when an oncoming driver waves you across,c:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before starting the turn
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is clear and you can complete the turn safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection,b:Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked,c:Stop completely
note: A flashing red light means stop, then continue only when the way is clear.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the proper response?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and drive to a safe place to stop.,b:Turn off your headlights and stop immediately in the travel lane.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and continue at the same speed.
note: Loss of power steering makes steering heavier; reduce speed and carefully pull off the road to a safe area to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a steady red traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop; you may turn right unless a sign prohibits it.,b:Drive through the intersection if no other vehicles are present.,c:Proceed unless a police officer is nearby.,d:Slow down and roll through if the way seems clear.
note: A steady red light requires a full stop. Unless prohibited by sign, you may turn right after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass on a two-way, two-lane street?
options: a:When you are able to partially drive on the shoulder,b:When your vehicle can reach the necessary passing speed only,c:Only if you can clearly see the road ahead and return to your lane before oncoming traffic appears
note: You may only pass when you can see clearly ahead, can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and it is legal and safe to do so.

question: A crossbuck sign at a roadway indicates:
options: a:No passing zone,b:School zone,c:Railroad crossing
note: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings and indicate drivers should yield to trains.

question: What is an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who checks mirrors regularly.,b:Someone who maintains eye contact with a passenger.,c:Someone who stares off the road,d:Someone who only watches the car ahead.
note: Being distracted by passengers, devices, or daydreaming reduces a driver’s ability to notice hazards and respond appropriately.

question: What does a green arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same as a circular green but only on one-way streets.,b:Traffic in the lane indicated may proceed but must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.,c:You may go straight only.
note: A green arrow gives you the right to make the movement indicated, but you must follow the arrow's direction.

question: What happens to your field of vision as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:It becomes more sensitive to peripheral movement.,b:It decreases,c:It increases dramatically.,d:It remains unchanged.
note: As speed rises your effective field of vision narrows, so you must be extra alert for hazards when driving faster.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Check rearview and side mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: Always check mirrors and your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes; signaling is also required.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over the shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the outside mirror on that side.
note: Mirrors may not show other vehicles in blind spots; always turn your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Only set the parking brake.,b:Leave the engine running briefly.,c:Leave the radio on to deter theft.,d:Turn off the engine
note: When unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition and remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a road means:
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not permitted
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and allow lane changes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Recommended speeds for inexperienced drivers only.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed for ideal conditions; you must slow below the limit when conditions require.,c:Potential driving speeds for the area only.,d:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limits show the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust lower when conditions are unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Look in your side mirror for traffic and turn on your directional signal.,b:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.
note: Always check mirrors, use your signal, and glance over the shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check blind spots.

question: When should you signal?
options: a:Only at intersections,b:Changing lanes,c:Only when making major turns
note: Always use signals when changing lanes, entering traffic from driveways/alleys, or pulling in/out of parking spaces to communicate intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers when entering traffic?
options: a:Only when they are on a road to your left,b:Only when your signal is green,c:When entering from a garage
note: Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic when entering from private property such as garages, alleys, or driveways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a sudden stop in the middle of the intersection.,b:Be prepared to stop safely; do not speed up to beat the red light.,c:Accelerate to beat the red.,d:Continue without changing speed in all cases.
