note: A steady yellow warns the light will turn red soon; slow and stop if it is safe to do so rather than accelerating to beat the light.

question: If your vehicle with ABS begins to skid on a slippery surface, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the gas pedal,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger,c:Pump the brakes repeatedly
note: With ABS, press firmly and hold the brake; the system will rapidly modulate braking so you can steer.

question: For persons age 21 or older, what BAC is illegal to drive at or above?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Drivers 21 and older are legally impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin slowing down as you exit a highway?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane,b:On the main road just before the exit lane,c:Only when you see a toll booth
note: Enter the exit lane well in advance; do not slow down on the main travel lanes before moving into the exit lane.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but not using emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in the center of the road.,b:Continue driving normally; you do not need to clear a path.,c:Pull over immediately and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: If an emergency vehicle is following but not using siren or lights, you are not required to clear the way; continue your normal driving.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, what is recommended?
options: a:Keep driving and listen to loud music.,b:Stop and rest every two hours or when drowsy.,c:Do arm exercises without stopping.,d:Drive with one eye closed occasionally.
note: Take regular breaks—about every two hours—or stop for rest if you become drowsy; never drive while fatigued.

question: What device is sometimes used on highways to indicate which lanes to use for turning?
options: a:Stop signs in the middle of the road.,b:Flashing red lights only.,c:Lane-use arrows painted on pavement or on overhead signs.,d:White lines on the side of the road.
note: Arrows (on signs or pavement) direct drivers into the proper lanes for left or right turns and for through traffic.

question: Extra caution is required when approaching a pedestrian carrying a white cane because:
options: a:They are likely blind or visually impaired,b:They are a police officer,c:They are deaf
note: White canes or guide dogs indicate blindness or visual impairment; yield and be prepared to stop.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, you should:
options: a:Stop at a safe distance and look for a train,b:Slow down and look for a train,c:Look for a train then speed up to clear the crossing
note: When warning lights are flashing, stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until signals stop.

question: When driving in bad weather, how should you adjust following distance?
options: a:Keep the same following distance as in good weather,b:Increase your following distance,c:Decrease your following distance
note: Increase following distance in rain, snow, or other adverse conditions to allow more time to stop.

question: Defensive driving is best defined as:
options: a:Getting ahead of poor drivers in traffic,b:Following the vehicle ahead closely to anticipate stops,c:Identifying dangerous situations and taking steps to avoid accidents
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking actions to prevent crashes.

question: If you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazards and keep driving.,b:Speed up to avoid it.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with sirens or lights, pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.

question: If a transit bus signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Yield and allow the bus to merge safely,b:Honk to let the driver know you're there,c:Speed up to pass before the bus merges
note: Yield to transit vehicles re-entering traffic after passenger loading; change lanes, slow, or stop as needed to let them merge safely.

question: What is the best practice to ensure safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, walk behind and around your vehicle to check for children, pets, and objects you cannot see from the driver seat.

question: Solid white stop lines painted across traffic lanes indicate:
options: a:In curves and on hills,b:Where drivers must stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks,c:Next to churches and schools
note: Stop lines mark the exact location where drivers must stop at intersections or crosswalks.

question: What is the most common cause of hydroplaning?
options: a:Frequent sudden stops.,b:Driving too fast for wet road conditions.,c:Making sudden turns.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a film of water; excessive speed on wet roads greatly increases the risk.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:
options: a:Keep the rear tires against the curb,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb
note: Turning the wheels away from the curb will make the car roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver shows the left arm and hand extended upward, what does that hand signal indicate?
options: a:Turn right.,b:Continue straight ahead.,c:Turn left.
note: A left arm extended upward from the driver indicates an intention to turn right when using hand signals.
